title: The 50 states: capitals and statehood, in order
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Fifty states, each with a capital and a birthday. Learned in order of statehood, the list tells the story of how the country grew: thirteen states on the Atlantic coast, then a march west across the continent, then Alaska and Hawaii in 1959.

How to hold it: Chunk by era. The order of statehood has natural breaks: the original thirteen; the states of the early republic (1791 to 1821); the westward growth before and during the Civil War (1836 to 1867); the West (1876 to 1912); and the last two in 1959. Learn one era in groups of about five, then close the book and recall it. For the capitals, link a picture to each pair (Baton Rouge, a red stick, standing in a bayou), and use a map as a memory palace, tracing the order of statehood with your finger. Come back on day 1, 3, 7 and 21.
This list has 50 items. Answer below, then check — the practice button generates fresh questions from the list itself.
